assessment.nobel_worthiness: Information design has supplied a powerful, general framework for strategic communication and market design.
assessment.attribution: Bergemann, Kamenica, and Morris are central architects of the theoretical framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach is well developed, widely used across theory and applied fields, and has generated a substantial body of follow-on work.
uncertainties: The contribution spans related models rather than a single sharply bounded discovery.
The appropriate division of credit within the broader literature remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity transformed modern trade theory and empirical work on trade, productivity, and welfare.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplied the foundational selection model, while Helpman and Redding made major complementary contributions to its extension and use.
assessment.maturity: The framework has had durable theoretical and empirical influence over two decades.
uncertainties: Credit is difficult because the research program includes many important contributors.
Empirical magnitudes and policy implications remain model-dependent.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work fundamentally clarified how technology, tasks, and trade shocks reshape local labour markets and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn, and Hanson have distinct and highly visible contributions to the core empirical research program.
assessment.maturity: Its methods and findings have been extensively tested and have strongly influenced public debate and subsequent research.
uncertainties: The relative importance of trade versus technological change varies across settings.
The broad contribution overlaps with important work by other labour economists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on fairness, reciprocity, and inequity aversion changed economic modeling of incentives and strategic behaviour.
assessment.attribution: Fehr and Falk produced foundational experimental evidence, and Schmidt made central theoretical contributions with Fehr.
assessment.maturity: The ideas are mature, broadly incorporated into theory, experiments, and organizational economics.
uncertainties: Experimental regularities can depend on institutions and framing.
Credit overlaps with the wider behavioural and experimental economics literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods became indispensable tools for empirical research with persistent outcomes and unobserved heterogeneity.
assessment.attribution: Arellano, Blundell, and Bond are directly identified with the principal estimators and their development.
assessment.maturity: The methods are longstanding, exceptionally influential, and their properties are well understood.
uncertainties: Applied use can be fragile under weak instruments and specification choices.
The contribution is methodological and may compete with other major econometric foundations.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and measurement made adverse selection in insurance markets empirically tractable and policy relevant.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav, and Salanie have each made central contributions to the modern evidence and framework.
assessment.maturity: A large subsequent literature has applied and refined these insights across insurance markets.
uncertainties: Findings differ substantially across insurance products and institutional contexts.
Attribution is broad because foundational theoretical work predates this program.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Political-economy analysis of institutions, accountability, and fiscal policy has reshaped understanding of how policy is formed.
assessment.attribution: Persson, Tabellini, and Besley are leading and complementary contributors to the listed research program.
assessment.maturity: The work has accumulated over decades and supports a mature theoretical and empirical literature.
uncertainties: Causal empirical claims about institutions are intrinsically difficult to isolate.
The field is broad, making a bounded prize citation and credit allocation challenging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Axiomatic models of ambiguity supplied rigorous alternatives to subjective expected utility and influenced finance, macroeconomics, and decision theory.
assessment.attribution: Gilboa and Epstein are foundational figures, with Marinacci a major contributor to formalization and development.
assessment.maturity: The theories are established and have produced a deep literature and important applications.
uncertainties: There is no single universally accepted behavioral model of ambiguity.
The empirical distinctiveness and quantitative relevance of competing ambiguity models remain debated.
